clue.text: Where apples found, it's said, one has an advantage

indicators.note: it's said tells us the phrase is to be heard rather than read, so its sound gives the entry

parts.note: apples are found in cider, the drink pressed from them

explanation.surface: A riddle about apples and the advantage someone holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with inside knowledge of an organisation enjoys an advantage over outsiders.

clue.text: Uplifting Japanese healing absorbing indefinite number, so darker

indicators.note: absorbing means the turned word takes the number into itself
in a down clue, uplifting means the healing word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: Reiki is a Japanese healing practice of laying on hands
n is the mathematician's symbol for an unspecified number

explanation.surface: Japanese healing that is uplifting turns out, oddly, to make things darker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uplifting' turns REIKI into IKIER, and 'absorbing' puts N inside it after the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Inkier is the comparative of inky, more black like ink, hence darker.

clue.text: Guarantee fatty swipes last of dinner

indicators.note: swipes means grabs and takes in, so the fatty word holds the letter

parts.note: suety means full of suet, the hard fat used in puddings

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word dinner

explanation.surface: A fatty diner pinches the end of someone's dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A surety is a pledge or person standing as security, a guarantee for a debt or appearance.

clue.text: Bundle of money raised to cover errant lover in court, primarily — this deciding who gets it?

indicators.note: to cover means the turned word goes around the rest
in a down clue, raised means the bundle word is read upwards

parts.note: a wad is a thick roll of banknotes

indicators.note: errant means wandering astray, so the letters are rearranged
primarily picks the first letters of in and court

explanation.surface: A wad of cash is raised to cover an unfaithful lover in court, with the law deciding who gets it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' turns the bundle upwards, 'errant' scrambles the lover with the court initials, and 'to cover' wraps one round the other. 'Cover' tempts as an anagram signal but means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Divorce law governs how a separating couple's money and property are split, deciding who gets the bundle.

clue.text: Dog runs on

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
over can mean on, as in a lecture on or over a subject

explanation.surface: A dog runs on and on.
explanation.definitionFit: Rover is a stock name for a pet dog, used to stand for any dog.

clue.text: Having touched base, 7 behind swimmer

indicators.note: touched means slightly mad, so the letters of base go crazy

parts.note: 7 is AMERICAN, and the American word for one's behind is ass

explanation.surface: Having touched base, an American's behind is a swimmer's.
explanation.walkthrough: 7-down is AMERICAN, so '7 behind' means the American word for a backside; the 'touched base' of baseball is misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea bass is an edible fish, so it swims.

clue.text: Roaming as cousins, carefree

indicators.note: roaming means wandering around, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Cousins roaming about without a care.
explanation.definitionFit: Sans souci is French borrowed into English meaning without worry, carefree.

clue.text: Cutter says more in conversation

indicators.note: in conversation means as spoken aloud, so the entry sounds like the phrase

parts.note: someone who says more adds to what was said

explanation.surface: A cutter says more when chatting.
explanation.definitionFit: An adze is an axe-like tool with an arched blade for cutting and shaping wood.

clue.text: Gray as a part of 17 down, say, whose unfinished elegy criminal pans out

definitions.text: Gray as a part of 17 down, say

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order and rearranged
unfinished means the word elegy loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Thomas Gray's unfinished elegy is sold off by a criminal who pans it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfinished' trims ELEGY to ELEG, and 'out' rearranges ELEG with CRIMINALPANS. The poet Gray of the Elegy is a false path; 'gray' is the US spelling, like COLOR in 17-down COLORADO.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing gray for grey, or color for colour, is an example of spelling as used in the United States.

clue.text: First of six quickies — they're out of this world!

indicators.note: First of picks the opening letter of the word six

parts.note: in cricket, quickies are fast bowlers, also called pacemen

explanation.surface: Six fast bowlers, out of this world.
explanation.definitionFit: Spacemen are astronauts or aliens, figures from outer space and literally out of this world.

clue.text: Nureyev or I keep holding back ballet company

indicators.note: back means the held letters read backwards
holding means the answer sits inside the run of words

explanation.surface: Nureyev or I keep holding back from a ballet company.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards through 'nureyeV OR I Keep'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kirov is the St Petersburg ballet company now called the Mariinsky, which Nureyev once danced with.

clue.text: 11 extreme characters, revolutionary, capturing leader of unstable nation

indicators.note: capturing means the shuffled letters close around a letter
revolutionary means turning things over, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the number written in words is eleven, not the cross-reference
a and z are the characters at the two ends of the alphabet

indicators.note: leader of picks the first letter of the word unstable

explanation.surface: A revolutionary group captures the leader of an unstable nation.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' looks like a cross-reference to 11-across but is the number ELEVEN. 'Revolutionary' shuffles ELEVEN with A and Z, and 'capturing' puts U inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Venezuela is a South American country, a nation.

clue.text: See 19
Exhaust, something on 7 car?

definitions.meaning: to exhaust is to wear out or fatigue
7 is AMERICAN, and an American car runs on ..., the US spelling of tyres

explanation.definitionFit: To tire is to exhaust; tire is also the American spelling of the rubber tyre on a wheel.

clue.text: Random tests making mark on 7 bank orders

parts.note: a spot is a mark or blemish
7 is AMERICAN, and the American spelling of cheques is checks

explanation.surface: Random tests on American bank orders, making a mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot checks are inspections made at random without warning.

clue.text: Compound, where Shed and Paul found drunk, getting in after midnight?

indicators.note: getting in means the shuffled letters go inside the time word

parts.note: after midnight is late, the question mark showing it is loose

indicators.note: drunk means the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: The setter Paul and Shed are found drunk, getting home after midnight.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul is the setter himself; 'drunk' scrambles the two names and 'getting in' sets them inside the time word. Note the British spelling, against the American theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead sulphate is a chemical compound, a white salt of lead.

clue.text: Go crazy wriggling nose into 7 confection

indicators.note: into means the wriggled letters are placed inside the confection

parts.note: 7 is AMERICAN, and the American spelling of doughnut is donut

indicators.note: wriggling means twisting about, so the letters of nose are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wriggling one's nose into an American doughnut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wriggling' scrambles the nose and 'into' sets it in the US-spelt doughnut. Doing one's nut is British slang for flying into a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: To do one's nut is British slang for losing one's temper, going crazy.

clue.text: See 7
A party's undertone (7) reaching 7 river

parts.note: read as under tone: tone in the American spelling gives color, which sits under the rest
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A party's undertone reaching an American river.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'undertone' as under + tone: the party goes under the American-spelt tone in this down entry, so the British spelling with OU is wrong here. 'Reaching' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: The Colorado is a major river of the American Southwest, flowing through the Grand Canyon.

clue.text: Heroes reduced pain in amoebae, say

indicators.note: in means the shortened pain word sits inside the organisms

parts.note: amoebae are examples of protists, single-celled organisms

indicators.note: reduced means the word for pain loses its last letter

parts.note: agony is intense pain

explanation.surface: Heroes reduce the pain suffered by amoebae.
explanation.definitionFit: Protagonists are the leading characters of a story, its heroes.

clue.text: Having turned up, leaders in blue lingerie instantly focus (7) to force government initiative

indicators.note: having turned means the word up is read backwards
leaders in picks the first letters of blue, lingerie and instantly

parts.note: 7 is AMERICAN, and a focus is a centre, spelt center in American
to prise is to force open with a lever

explanation.surface: Blue lingerie that turns up becomes an instant focus.
explanation.definitionFit: Public enterprise is business run by the state, a government initiative rather than a private one.

clue.text: Shrink from bacterium, turning tail, under bottom of sewer

indicators.note: under places the bacterium beneath the letter in this down entry
bottom of picks the final letter of the word sewer
turning tail means the last pair of letters swap round

parts.note: E. coli is a gut bacterium

explanation.surface: Shrinking from a bacterium that turns tail at the bottom of a sewer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning tail' moves the L at the tail of ECOLI to the very end, giving ECOIL, which goes under R.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoil from something is to shrink back from it in fear or disgust.

clue.text: Kitty flips, seeing ring

indicators.note: flips means the kitty word is turned over and read backwards

parts.note: a pool is a shared fund of money, a kitty

explanation.surface: The cat flips on seeing a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A loop is a ring-shaped curve or circle.

clue.text: Fresh in retirement, put out about the limits of youth finding very little accommodation

indicators.note: in retirement means going back, so the word fresh is read backwards

parts.note: fresh means new

indicators.note: about means the extinguishing word goes around the edge letters

parts.note: to douse a fire is to put it out

indicators.note: the limits of picks the first and last letters of the word youth

explanation.surface: Fresh in retirement, someone puts out the young, finding very little accommodation.
explanation.definitionFit: A Wendy house is a toy playhouse for children, accommodation on a tiny scale.

clue.text: King had one hand, finally, on paper

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word hand

parts.note: a ream is a quantity of paper, 500 sheets

explanation.surface: A king held one hand on paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The King is Martin Luther King, who said 'I have a dream'.
explanation.definitionFit: Martin Luther King's famous 1963 speech declared he had a vision of the future.

clue.text: Egg emu voted to gobble up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the held letters read from the bottom
to gobble means the letters are swallowed inside the words

explanation.surface: An emu voted to gobble up an egg.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovum is a female reproductive cell, an egg.

clue.text: I send over daring man, old politician Cyrus, getting ahead

indicators.note: send over means the man's name is turned back to front

parts.note: Dan Dare is a daring British comic-strip space hero
Cyrus Vance was US Secretary of State under President Carter

explanation.surface: I send over a daring man, the old politician Cyrus, to get ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Send over' turns DAN into NAD. Dan Dare was the hero of the British comic Eagle, so the 'daring man' is Dan.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in advance means doing it ahead of time, getting ahead.

clue.text: Little room with love, one between your legs?

parts.note: a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery
love is zero in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: A little love room, with a cheeky question about what is between your legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellist holds the instrument upright between the knees to play it.

clue.text: Cat returning to cross river, came across eyelet

indicators.note: to cross means the turned word stretches across the river letter
returning means the cat word is read backwards

parts.note: mog is British slang for a cat
to meet someone is to come across them

explanation.surface: A cat turns back to cross a river and comes across an eyelet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' turns MOG into GOM, which 'to cross' splits around R.
explanation.definitionFit: A grommet is a metal or rubber ring lining a hole, an eyelet.

clue.text: Show false claim about 7

indicators.note: about means the shuffled letters go around the country abbreviation
false means the word claim is reworked into a different arrangement

parts.note: 7 is AMERICAN, and US is short for United States

explanation.surface: A show makes a false claim about America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'False' gives MICAL, which 'about' wraps around US.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical is a stage show with songs, such as one on Broadway.
